units.title: All

exercises.question: Hello
exercises.explain: Bonjour literally means "good day" and works any time before evening. After dark, switch to Bonsoir.

exercises.question: Thank you
exercises.explain: Merci stands alone. To say what for, add pour: merci pour tout, "thanks for everything".

exercises.question: Goodbye
exercises.explain: Au revoir means "until we see each other again" — revoir is re- (again) + voir (to see).

exercises.question: Water
exercises.explain: Eau is feminine: l'eau, une eau. The silent final letters (e-a-u for one sound) are typical of French spelling.

exercises.question: Cat
exercises.explain: Chat is masculine (le chat). A female cat is une chatte — the final consonant becomes audible.

exercises.question: House
exercises.explain: Maison is feminine: la maison. Chez moi ("at my place") is the more common way to say "home" in speech.

exercises.question: Please
exercises.explain: Literally "if it pleases you". Drop to s'il te plait with someone you'd address as tu.

exercises.question: Yes
exercises.explain: For a positive answer to a negative question ("Isn't it?" — "Actually, yes"), French uses si instead of oui.

exercises.question: The cat is black
exercises.explain: Le marks chat as masculine. Adjectives usually follow the noun in French: chat noir, not noir chat.

exercises.question: I eat bread
exercises.explain: Du is the partitive article, "some" bread. French can't drop it the way English drops "some" — je mange pain is ungrammatical.

exercises.question: She is beautiful
exercises.explain: Belle is the feminine form of beau. Masculine nouns before a vowel sound use a third form, bel (un bel homme).

exercises.question: I like music
exercises.explain: Je elides to J' before a vowel sound. La stays because musique is feminine and needs an article even for a general like.

exercises.question: Type what you hear
exercises.audio: Bonjour
exercises.explain: The on in Bonjour is a nasal vowel with no English equivalent — air through the nose, not an "n" sound at the end.

exercises.question: Type what you hear
exercises.audio: Comment allez-vous
exercises.explain: Comment allez-vous is the formal "how are you". The inversion (allez-vous instead of vous allez) is what marks it as a question here, not just word order.

exercises.question: Type what you hear
exercises.audio: Bonne nuit
exercises.explain: Bonne nuit is only for parting at bedtime. During the evening itself, the greeting is Bonsoir, not Bonne nuit.

units.tip: French greetings and thanks don't translate word for word — s'il vous plait is literally "if it pleases you". Learn the phrase, not just the words in it.
